newsitem.title: USA: PJM sees pool-wide power transmission rates Apr 1
newsitem.headline: PJM sees pool-wide power transmission rates Apr 1

text.p: The Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool said it aimed to implement on April 1 a single set of rates for all power providers who use its members' transmission networks.
This is one month later than a recent ruling by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), which late Friday said a new set of transmission rates would take effect from March 1.

PJM, in a letter sent Tuesday, told FERC its members and marketers needed more time to become more familiar with the new fees, and that they would instead continue to offer transmission services using their own rates.

PJM's move followed Friday's FERC order, which was in turn responding to a request by PJM for a ruling on various transmission issues that would give all electricity suppliers equal access to the pool's high-voltage lines and other transmission services.
Those issues include assessment of transmission prices during "congestion" periods, when energy demand is high or transmission capacity in PJM is tight.
FERC said it supports the implementation of PECO Energy Co's plan as a temporary measure, which calls for congestion tariffs be paid for by all PJM users through a single fee. PECO is a PJM member.
A rival proposal sponsored by the Supporting Companies Group, comprising all PJM utility members except PECO, argues for users to pay for congestion fees on particular
transmission paths they move energy on.

The group's plan is considered more compatible with FERC's goals in deregulating the power industry, but FERC said there are still technical issues which the Supporting Companies Group need to resolve to make its plan workable.
In 1995, FERC called for utilities to devise plans to allow equal access on their transmission systems to other electricity suppliers including marketers and independent power producers.
The policy aimed to further the goal of more competition and lower rates in the domestic electricity industry.
Currently, PJM has 10 Mid-Atlantic utilities as members
which include Atlantic City Energy Co, Baltimore Gas and Electric Co, three GPU Inc subsidiaries
Metropolitan Edison Co, Pennsylvania Electric Co, and Jersey Cental Power & Light Co, PECO Energy Co, Pennsylvania Power & Light Co, Potomac Electric Power Co and Public Service Electric and Gas Co
The roster would likely be expanded in a March 31 meeting when eligible parties could apply for membership, PJM said.
